newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CELTIC FANS ANGRY AS BURNS IS SACKED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CELTIC FANS ANGRY AS BURNS IS SACKED.

text.p: Glasgow Celtic manager Tommy Burns paid the price of the inevitable Scottish championship success of bitter city rivals Rangers when he was sacked by the club on Friday.

Burns' three-year reign came to an end amid stormy scenes at the club's Parkhead ground where several hundred fans directed their anger at chief executive Fergus McCann for what they perceived to be the shoddy treatment of one of Celtic's most loyal servants.
The 40-year-old had been a Celtic player for 14 years and was recruited by McCann from Kilmarnock in 1994 as the man who could stop Rangers' domination of Scottish soccer.

Neither Burns nor McCann made any immediate comment, but Celtic club spokesman Peter McClean said: "Celtic would like to thank Tommy Burns for his servce and it is the club's intention he should stay on as a consultant but as yet he has not indicated a decision to us."

Astonshingly, the move came less than 48 hours before Sunday's league match wth Hibernan. Although Celtic need to win all three of their remaining games and hope Rangers lose all of theirs, the championship race was mathematically still not over.
Though Burns led Celtic to a Scottish Cup triumph in 1995, he failed to deliver the ultimate prize of the title.

On Monday, Rangers need just one point from their home match with Motherwell to wrap up a ninth successive league success to equal Celtic's record feat achieved under legendary coach Jock Stein betweeen 1966 and 1974.
Speculation had been rife for weeks that Burns, who had a strained personal relationship with McCann, could be on his way out of Parkhead.
It intensified after Celtic lost the Old Firm derby to Rangers in the league at the beginning of March which all but sealed the destination of the title.
The situation worsened when his side were knocked out of the Scottish Cup semifinals by first division side Falkirk last week, thus losing their last chance of an honour.

Burns was called to Parkhead on Friday night and ruthlessly dismissed after a short board meeting. Burns had indicated he would wait untl the summer before deciding his future and only last week McCann said he would stay as manager at least until the end of the season.

Celtic have made enormous strides off the pitch since mcCann took control of what was then a financially ailing club in 1994. The club are now in a healthy state, but the board felt that success off the pitch was not being met with enough succeess on it.

Celtic may offer the job to a well-known European football coach such as Englishman Bobby Rbson, whom McCann offered the job to in 1994. Johann Cruyff and Kevin Keegan have also been linked with the post.
